posts.title: Ionic or covalent? Spot it in 2 seconds.
altText: Reel, Lock It In number 3, GCSE Chemistry, Bonding. Question: ionic or covalent? Two cards side by side. Ionic: made from a metal and a non-metal, electrons transferred, for example sodium chloride, NaCl. Covalent: usually non-metals only, electrons shared, for example water, H2O. Text: Ionic, the metal gives electrons to the non-metal, making ions that attract. Covalent, non-metal atoms share pairs of electrons. Write the formula, then look for a metal. Memory trick: metal in it? Usually ionic. Only non-metals? Usually covalent. Ammonium is an exception. Ends on: Save this. Lock it in. Follow for Lock It In number 4.

platforms.label: Instagram Reel
platforms.caption:
Ionic or covalent? At GCSE, ionic bonding is usually between a metal and a non-metal: the metal gives electrons to the non-metal, making ions that attract each other, as in sodium chloride. Covalent bonding is between non-metal atoms, which share pairs of electrons, as in water.

Memory trick: metal in it? Usually ionic. Only non-metals? Usually covalent. Exception to know: ammonium compounds like NH₄Cl are ionic with no metal.
